thesis: Snowflake reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 2 September 2026: product revenue of $1.49B, up 37% year over year, total revenue of $1.55B and adjusted EPS of $0.62 against reported consensus of $1.48B and $0.45, and it raised full-year product revenue guidance to $6.07B from the $5.84B given in May, with non-GAAP operating margin guidance lifted to 14.5% from 13.5%; Q3 product revenue is guided to $1.59B. Both metrics are reported here: on a GAAP basis the quarter was still a net loss of $191.7M, or $0.55 per share, narrower than the $297.9M / $0.89 loss a year earlier, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded more than 400bps to 15%. Shares rose about 21% on 3 September to a new 52-week high on 4.95x average volume. The strongest counter-argument is that the company remains GAAP-unprofitable while the stock now trades at a five-year high, so the multiple has run ahead of reported earnings; the disclosed figures answer it, because the GAAP loss narrowed roughly 36% year over year, non-GAAP margin expanded over 400bps and product growth accelerated for a third consecutive quarter, so the loss is shrinking against accelerating revenue rather than widening. Management attributed about half of the acceleration to AI products, with the CoCo coding agent at 9,100 accounts, up over 2,000 in the quarter. This suggests the acceleration is being driven by disclosed product adoption rather than by pricing or one-off items.
invalidation: product revenue growth decelerates from the guided ~36% full-year pace, or the $6.07B FY2027 product revenue / 14.5% non-GAAP operating margin guidance is cut at the next quarterly report

thesis: Held position. Dell reported fiscal Q2 2027 on 1 September 2026: record revenue of $47.0B, up 58% year over year, and record non-GAAP diluted EPS of $7.04, up 203%, with adjusted EPS reported as $2.17 above the $4.87 consensus and revenue $2.16B above estimates. Infrastructure Solutions Group revenue rose 89% to $31.8B; the company booked $60.9B of AI server orders in the quarter and exited with a record $95.0B AI backlog, taking trailing-twelve-month AI orders to $131.7B. Dell raised full-year fiscal 2027 guidance by $25B to a $192.0B revenue midpoint, about 70% growth, and lifted non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance to a $25.50 midpoint. The stock is at a new 52-week high, up 25.4% over the 60-day window on 3.4x average volume. The strongest counter-argument is that the $95B figure is backlog — orders, not recognised revenue — and the company has not disclosed the timing of its conversion, so a backlog number can flatter a quarter it never reaches the P&L in; that is answered concretely by the fact that Dell raised recognised-revenue guidance by $25B and EPS guidance to $25.50 at the same time, so the near-term earnings effect is itself a company-disclosed forward figure rather than an inference from backlog. A litigation check this run found an ERISA suit over the Dell Inc. 401(k) plan filed in 2026 and WSOU patent appeals docketed at the Federal Circuit, but no scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline within the next ~90 days, so neither is flagged.
invalidation: the $192.0B revenue / $25.50 EPS fiscal 2027 guidance is reduced, or the AI backlog stops growing and quarterly AI orders fall materially below the $60.9B booked this quarter
sources: Justia docket (WSOU Investments LLC v. Dell Technologies Inc., Fed. Cir. 26-2087): https://dockets.justia.com/docket/circuit-courts/cafc/26-2087

thesis: Held position. Microsoft's most recent reported quarter, covered in early-August 2026 press, showed Microsoft Cloud revenue of $59.3B, up 27% year over year, Azure revenue passing $100B on an annualised basis and Microsoft 365 Copilot passing 30 million paid seats; Citi, Wolfe Research, Cantor Fitzgerald and Piper Sandler each raised price targets after the fiscal Q4 report. The stock is up 31.9% over the 60-day window and sits 7.4% below its 52-week high. The strongest counter-argument is the pending securities class action alleging Microsoft made materially false or misleading statements about Copilot adoption and Azure performance between 1 May 2025 and 28 January 2026 while concealing technical, organisational and interoperability problems — an allegation that goes directly at the numbers this thesis relies on. It does not change the read, because the figures cited above are the company's own disclosures for a quarter that falls entirely after the alleged class period ends, so the suit contests prior-period statements rather than the currently reported run-rate. The lead-plaintiff deadline in that action was 11 August 2026 and has passed; this run's research found no scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days, so active_litigation is not flagged. Note that the quarterly figures here were read in secondary coverage of the earnings release rather than in the release itself.
invalidation: Microsoft Cloud growth decelerates materially from the reported 27%, Copilot paid-seat growth stalls, or the securities class action produces a disclosed adverse ruling or settlement charge
sources: National Law Review (Levi & Korsinsky notice, MSFT class action): https://natlawreview.com/press-releases/msft-shareholder-alert-august-11-2026-lead-plaintiff-deadline-microsoft

thesis: The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF began trading on 6 August 2026 and closed today at a new low for its short life, at $23.00 against a 52-week low of $23.33 — the mechanical near-52-week-low trigger. It is an actively managed thematic fund holding companies deriving at least 50% of revenue from optical transceivers, lasers, silicon photonics, optical interconnects and related areas, with a 0.65% gross expense ratio; there is no company-disclosed catalyst behind the move, and no fund-specific disclosure was found. The decline is a sector move: the AI-optics complex it tracks sold off across the same window, with Coherent down about 36% over three months and Applied Optoelectronics down 18.6% over the 60-day window on this run's own measurements. This suggests the fund's new low reflects the drawdown in its underlying theme rather than anything disclosed about the vehicle. That is a sector-wide rather than company-specific cause, and with only 21 daily bars of history the volume baseline is thin, so this is not a basis for a position.
invalidation: a company-specific, disclosed catalyst emerges for the fund's largest holdings, or the optics complex stabilises and the fund reclaims its 6 August starting level

thesis: Astera Labs reported record Q2 2026 results on 4 August 2026, beating on both revenue and earnings, and guided fiscal Q3 2026 to $540-560M of revenue, roughly 40% sequential growth at the midpoint, with EPS guidance of $1.16-1.21. The shares nonetheless fell about 12% the day after and have kept falling: down 34.6% over the 60-day window, and 43.4% below the 52-week high. Coverage read this run attributes the fall to positioning and valuation rather than to disclosed deterioration — the results were preceded by a sharp run-up, and the reported Q2 weakness was higher operating expense from continued product-roadmap investment, not a demand shortfall. Competitive pressure is the named counter-case: Marvell, Cisco and Credo are expanding in the same AI-interconnect space, and Marvell introduced its Teralynx T100 102.4 Tbps switch silicon in June 2026. That counter-case cannot be settled from what this run read — no source quantifies any share loss, and the company's own guidance points the other way — so the evidence is genuinely unresolved. The move is explained as sentiment- and valuation-driven rather than as disclosed fundamental deterioration, which is what caps this rating.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the guided $540M floor, or management withdraws the ~40% sequential growth outlook or discloses share loss in the Scorpio/interconnect ramp

thesis: Rocket Lab reported Q2 2026 on 10-11 August 2026 with record revenue of $234M, up 62% year over year, and a $2.36B backlog, but the shares fell on the same report and are down 31.5% over the 60-day window, 57.9% below the 52-week high. The company-disclosed item behind the fall is the Neutron schedule: Rocket Lab still expects the rocket to reach the launchpad in Q4 2026 but stopped short of reaffirming a launch before year-end, with CEO Peter Beck saying the window for an end-year launch is narrowing and that the current work is risk trading between the timing of the first launch and how quickly the company can scale to its tenth. The evidence is genuinely offsetting and this run could not resolve it: record revenue and a large backlog on one side, an unquantified slip in the single programme the equity story rests on and no disclosed new target date on the other. This suggests the market is pricing execution risk on Neutron ahead of the reported financial momentum, and with no launch date disclosed there is no dated event to underwrite an entry against.
invalidation: Rocket Lab discloses a firm Neutron first-flight date, or conversely confirms the first launch has slipped out of Q4 2026 into 2027

thesis: Corning is down 25.1% over the 60-day window and 46.2% below its 52-week high. Three disclosed or reported items sit behind it. Corning beat consensus on both revenue and earnings for Q2 2026 but guided Q3 slightly below elevated consensus, which coverage read this run ties to a single-day decline of more than 20%. Optical Communications, the AI-linked growth segment, grew 32% year over year to $2.07B, decelerating from 36% the prior quarter. And in August, reports that Apple had scrapped its planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone knocked the shares again, with a five-session run taking about $24B off the market value. The evidence is mixed rather than resolved: the quarter itself beat, the guidance did not, and the Apple item is a customer decision reported by third parties rather than anything Corning disclosed. This suggests the de-rating is about the rate of change in the optical business and a lost specialty-glass programme rather than a step down in the current business, but this run could not settle which dominates.
invalidation: Corning guides Optical Communications growth back above the 32% year-over-year pace, or confirms the scale of any Apple specialty-glass volume loss in its next report

thesis: Intel is down 25.0% over the 60-day window and 35.7% below its 52-week high. The company-disclosed item is an equity raise: Intel priced a secondary offering of 210.5 million new shares at $95, lifting total proceeds to about $20B from an earlier $15B target, and coverage read this run attributes the late-August weakness to the resulting supply overhang. The rest of the recent move is explicitly macro: higher bond yields cut risk appetite in early September and pressured semiconductors broadly, with MU, SNDK, AMD and INTC all sliding together on 2 September. Coverage also references a 26% single-day drop on 2 August after disappointing quarterly results and projections, but this run did not read the results themselves and so does not characterise that print. The dominant identifiable causes here are a dilutive raise and a sector-wide de-rating rather than a company-specific operating catalyst, and the pieces this run could confirm do not resolve into a clear net read.
invalidation: the $20B offering is absorbed and Intel discloses foundry or product results that reverse the guidance disappointment behind the 2 August decline

thesis: Corcept Therapeutics reported Q2 2026 on 29-30 July 2026: revenue of $256.1M, up 32% year over year, split between $208.6M of Korlym and authorised generic revenue and $47.6M of Lifyorli (relacorilant) product revenue, and it raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.1-1.2B from a lower prior range. The company said more than 1,300 patients have started Lifyorli since FDA approval in the platinum-resistant ovarian cancer indication, with demand accelerating each month. The shares rose 20.8% after hours on that report, from a $92.95 close, and are up 23.1% over the 60-day window, now 10.7% below the 52-week high on well-below-average volume. The counter-case is regulatory: the FDA issued a Complete Response Letter on 31 December 2025 for relacorilant in hypertension secondary to hypercortisolism, and Corcept resubmitted a separate NDA for Cushing's syndrome in June 2026. That is a real negative, and while it concerns indications outside the two products now generating the disclosed revenue, this run could not establish whether an FDA action date on the resubmission falls before this position's next review, so it is not treated as settled.
invalidation: full-year revenue guidance is cut below the raised $1.1-1.2B range, Lifyorli's monthly patient-start growth stalls, or the resubmitted Cushing's syndrome NDA draws a second Complete Response Letter
sources: Corcept Q2 2026 press release (SEC Form 8-K exhibit): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001088856/000162828026050607/cort072926ex991pressrelease.htm

thesis: AST SpaceMobile is down 22.9% over the 60-day window and 53.6% below its 52-week high. Q2 2026, reported on the evening of 10 August 2026, missed on both lines: revenue of $31.5M against a $35.18M consensus, and an adjusted loss of $0.77 per share against an expected $0.26 loss, with the quarter including a $125.9M loss on involuntary conversion tied to the BB7 launch incident. The company maintained full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150-200M and reported pro forma liquidity above $3.7B as of 30 June. Two further items weighed: a $1.15B gross raise of 1.625% convertible senior notes in July 2026, whose convertible structure raised dilution concerns, and a 26 August selloff after SpaceX announced structural changes to its launch operations, given AST's dependence on third-party rockets. The evidence is offsetting and this run could not resolve it — a large liquidity position and unchanged revenue guidance against a wide earnings miss, a launch-related charge and an unquantified dependency on a competitor's launch capacity.
invalidation: AST SpaceMobile reaffirms or beats the $150-200M full-year revenue range on its next report, or conversely cuts it, and the launch-provider dependency is resolved with a disclosed multi-launch agreement

thesis: Coherent reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 12 August 2026 with EPS of $1.74 against a $1.58 consensus and revenue up 33.8% year over year to $2.046B against a $1.99B consensus, and guided fiscal Q1 EPS to $1.85-2.05 versus a $1.77 consensus. Despite that, the stock is down 21.2% over the 60-day window and roughly 36% over three months, and sits 39.9% below its 52-week high. Coverage read this run attributes the decline to two things: profit-taking after a seven-day run that had added roughly 71% to the market value, with a 14.2% single-day fall as traders unwound a crowded AI-optics position ahead of the print, and a $2B share issuance. That issuance inside the last ~90 days is why dilution_risk is flagged. The move is therefore explained as positioning and dilution rather than as disclosed operating deterioration — the reported quarter and the forward guidance both came in above consensus — and that framing, together with the flag, is what caps this rating rather than the fundamentals themselves.
invalidation: fiscal Q1 EPS lands below the guided $1.85 floor, or datacom/AI optical revenue growth decelerates from the reported 33.8% year-over-year pace

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics reported Q2 2026 on 6 August 2026: record revenue for a fifth consecutive quarter of $191.9M, up 86% year over year and slightly ahead of a ~$190M consensus, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.06 against a $0.01 consensus and non-GAAP net income of $5.5M. Both metrics are reported here, because they diverge: on a GAAP basis the quarter was a $22.8M net loss, and GAAP gross margin fell to 27.7% from 30.3% a year earlier, on higher operating expense and R&D and infrastructure investment. Q3 guidance was mixed against consensus — revenue of $255-290M versus roughly $278M expected, but EPS of $0.11-0.26 versus $0.28 expected. The stock is down 18.6% over the 60-day window and 57.0% below its 52-week high; the sharp late-August leg down followed an Equity Distribution Agreement signed 21 August 2026 for an at-the-market offering of up to $600M, about 5.7% of the equity value, which sent the shares down more than 12% pre-market on 24 August. That programme is why dilution_risk is flagged, and the flag is what caps this rating.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the guided $255M floor, GAAP gross margin erodes further from 27.7%, or the $600M ATM programme is drawn down materially at depressed prices

thesis: AMD reported Q2 2026 on 4 August 2026 with revenue of $11.536B, up 50% year over year, and Data Center revenue of $6.7B, up 107%, both ahead of expectations; management guided server CPU revenue to grow more than 80% year over year in the second half of 2026 and more than 70% in 2027. The shares still fell about 8.9% after hours and closed the next session down 7.0%, and are down 17.4% over the 60-day window, 22.0% below the 52-week high. The counter-case is specific and company-disclosed: gross margin guidance for Q3 was held flat at the same 56% as Q2, and coverage identifies that plateau, rather than the revenue beat, as the market's objection, alongside the observation that AMD's growth pace lags Nvidia's. This run could not settle that. Nothing in what was read explains what holds the margin flat while data-center revenue doubles, so the question of whether the mix is structurally dilutive or the flat guide is conservatism remains open, and the evidence is therefore unresolved rather than merely incomplete.
invalidation: gross margin is guided below 56%, or second-half server CPU revenue growth comes in under the stated 80% year-over-year pace

thesis: Marvell reported Q2 on 27-28 August 2026 with record quarterly revenue of $2.74B, up more than 36% year over year against a $2.71B consensus, and EPS of $0.94, beating on both lines, and raised its longer-term outlook. The shares nonetheless fell about 10% the following session and are down 16.2% over the 60-day window, 36.9% below the 52-week high. Coverage read this run frames the selloff as an expectations problem rather than a deterioration — investors wanted a larger beat after a substantial AI-driven run — with one specific complaint: Marvell gave limited detail on its fiscal 2028 outlook, damping sentiment after hopes that a Google partnership worth up to $12.2B in shares would lift earnings further. That counter-case was engaged and could not be settled here, because the missing fiscal 2028 detail is precisely what would settle it and the company has not disclosed it. This suggests the reaction reflects the gap between disclosed guidance and positioning rather than the reported results, but the evidence remains unresolved.
invalidation: Marvell's fiscal 2028 outlook, when disclosed, implies growth below the current pace, or the Google partnership's contribution is reduced or delayed

thesis: Lumentum reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 12 August 2026 with revenue of $1.006B, its first billion-dollar quarter, against a $987.7M consensus, and adjusted EPS of $3.23 against a $2.97 consensus; the stock rose 13.6% that day to close at $932.47, and multiple banks including Mizuho, JPMorgan, Raymond James, Citi and BNP Paribas raised targets, citing laser demand and margins. The shares are up 15.9% over the 60-day window and sit 22.0% below the 52-week high. Both metrics are not fully reconciled here, and that is the counter-case: one filing summary read this run describes 2026 revenue rising 83% alongside a large non-cash debt loss, and this run did not obtain the GAAP figure or the size of that charge, so the gap between the adjusted EPS quoted above and the GAAP result is unquantified. That is unresolved evidence rather than an absence of evidence, since a non-cash charge of unknown size sits against a clearly disclosed adjusted beat, and it is what caps this rating.
invalidation: the first billion-dollar revenue run-rate is not sustained in the next quarter, or the non-cash debt charge proves to reflect a financing structure that dilutes shareholders

thesis: Held position. The stock is up 16.8% over the 60-day window and sits 3.4% below its 52-week high, which is what triggered the screen. This run could not confirm the catalyst for that move: press referenced an Nvidia quarterly report on 26 August 2026, but no source read this run states its results, so nothing here characterises that print as a beat, a miss or a raise. The disclosed figures this run did read are for fiscal 2026 as a whole — revenue of $215.9B, up 65% year over year, with Data Center compute revenue up 59% on Blackwell demand and Data Center networking up 142%. Against that sits a substantial legal overhang: the US Supreme Court has allowed the shareholder class action over alleged misrepresentation of crypto-mining revenue in 2017-2018 to proceed, the Department of Justice has issued subpoenas in an antitrust probe, an antitrust investigation is open in China, and French antitrust charges have been brought. That counter-case was engaged and could not be settled — none of these matters has a disclosed scheduled ruling, hearing or compliance deadline within the next ~90 days, which is also why active_litigation is not flagged, but the absence of a date is not evidence about the outcome. The position still rests on the disclosed fiscal 2026 growth, with the most recent quarter unverified.
invalidation: Nvidia's most recent quarterly results, once confirmed, show Data Center growth decelerating materially, or any of the antitrust matters produces a disclosed remedy, fine or conduct restriction

thesis: Held position. Sandisk held an investor day on 13 August 2026 focused on long-term NAND, AI and customer-contract demand, where management gave long-term targets of double-digit revenue growth through 2030 and an 80% non-GAAP gross margin. Coverage read this run describes AI infrastructure demand keeping NAND supply very tight with strong pricing, and notes Bernstein raising its price target to $3,000 on an estimate that recent Sandisk agreements carry a floor price of roughly $0.29 per gigabyte. Against that, the stock is down 10.9% over the 60-day window and sits 34.2% below its 52-week high, even though it remains up over 500% across 2026. That gap is the counter-case and this run could not close it: no source read here identifies any disclosed deterioration — no guidance cut, no contract loss, no raise — that would account for a 34% drawdown from the high, and the most recent leg lower on 2 September was a sector move that took MU, SNDK, AMD and INTC down together. The targets themselves are also forward-looking rather than a completed event. The position is held on disclosed pricing and demand conditions, with the drawdown unexplained.
invalidation: NAND contract pricing rolls over from the ~$0.29/GB floor level described, or Sandisk's next quarterly report walks back the investor-day double-digit growth and 80% gross margin trajectory
